{{Short description|Croatian chemist (1936–2021)}}
'''Nenad Trinajstić''' (26 October 1936 – 27 August 2021) was a Croatian chemist and one of pioneers of the [[chemical graph theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal | author=Milan Randić| author-link=Milan Randić | title=Nenad Trinajstić – Pioneer of Chemical Graph Theory | journal=Croatica Chemica Acta | year=2004 | volume=77 | issue=1–2 | pages=1–15 | url=http://hrcak.srce.hr/index.php?show=clanak&id_clanak_jezik=151124 }}</ref>

==Life and work==
Trinajstić was born in [[Zagreb]]. He received M.Sc. and [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] degrees from the [[University of Zagreb]] based on work done at the [[University of Sheffield]] under John Murrell. His doctoral advisor was [[Milan Randić]]. From 1968 to 1970 he was a Postdoctoral fellow under [[Michael J. S. Dewar]] at the [[University of Texas]], [[Austin, Texas|Austin]] with whom he has published 16 papers.
He worked at [[Pliva]] and [[Ruđer Bošković Institute]] eventually becoming a full research professor in 1977 and from 2001 professor emeritus at the [[University of Zagreb]].<ref>{{Cite journal | author=N. Trinajstić | title=A Life in Science | year=2003 | journal=Internet Electron. J. Mol. Des | volume=2 | pages=413–434 | url=http://biochempress.com/Files/iejmd_2003_2_0413.pdf}}</ref>

His scientific interests are [[quantum chemistry]], [[mathematical chemistry]], [[chemoinformatics]], [[history of chemistry]] and philosophy of natural science. He wrote the first monograph on [[chemical graph theory]]<ref>N. Trinajstic. Chemical Graph Theory. Vols. 1,2. CRC Press: Boca Raton, Florida, 1983; 2nd Ed. 1992.</ref> and introduced several [[molecular descriptor]]s such as 3-dimensional [[Wiener index]]<ref>{{cite journal |author1=B. Bogdanov |author2=S. Nikolić |author3=N. Trinajstić | title=On the three-dimensional wiener number | journal=Journal of Mathematical Chemistry |  year=1989 | volume=3 | issue=3 | pages=299–309 | doi=10.1007/BF01169597|s2cid=119849884 }}</ref> and Zagreb indices (with Ivan Gutman),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=I. Gutman |author2=N. Trinajstić | title= Graph theory and molecular orbitals. Total φ-electron energy of alternant hydrocarbons | journal=Chemical Physics Letters |  year=1972 | volume=17 | issue=4 | pages=535–538 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(72)85099-1|bibcode=1972CPL....17..535G }}</ref> which are among the more studied topological indices. Independently of Jun-ichi Aihara, he introduced topological [[resonance energy]] as a reliable theory of [[aromaticity]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=I. Gutman |author2=M. Milun |author3=N. Trinajstić | title= Topological Definition of Resonance Energy | journal=MATCH – Commun. Math. Computer Chem |  year=1975 | volume=1 | pages=171–175}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=I. Gutman |author2=M. Milun |author3=N. Trinajstić | title= Graph Theory and Molecular Orbitals. XIX. Non–Parametric Resonance Energies of Arbitrary Conjugated Systems | journal= J. Am. Chem. Soc. |  year=1977 | volume=99 | issue=6 | pages=1692–1704 | doi=10.1021/ja00448a002}}</ref> In quantum chemistry he worked on semi-empirical [[molecular orbital theory]] and settling [[conjugated-circuit model]] on a firm quantum-mechanical basis.<ref>{{cite journal | author=S. Nikolić   | title= Nenad Trinajstić – curriculum vitae | journal=Croatica Chemica Acta |  year=2004 | volume=77 | issue=1–2 | pages=19–22 | url=http://hrcak.srce.hr/102640}}</ref> Trinajstić has published more than 500 scientific papers, about 150 technical papers and 12 books.

He was a full member of [[Croatian Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref name="hazu">{{cite web|url=http://info.hazu.hr/hr/clanovi_akademije/osobne_stranice/nenad_trinajstic|title=HAZU • Hrvatska akademija znanosti i umjetnosti - Nenad Trinajstić - Biografija|publisher=info.hazu.hr|accessdate=2015-02-11}}</ref> a member of [[International Academy of Mathematical Chemistry]]<ref name="iamc-online">{{cite web|url=http://www.iamc-online.org/members/index.htm|title=IAMC|publisher=iamc-online.org|accessdate=2015-02-11}}</ref> and was awarded the Mid–America State Universities Association Distinguished Foreign Scholar Award in 1986 and Croatian National Science Award in 2003. 

Trinajstić died on 27 August 2021 at the age of 85.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umro hrvatski kemičar, akademik Nenad Trinajstić|url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/umro-hrvatski-kemicar-akademik-nenad-trinajstic-1518560|access-date=2021-08-29|publisher=[[Večernji list]] |language=hr}}</ref>
